stanzas.sanskrit:
हिरण्याक्षे पोत्रिप्रवरवपुषा देव भवता
हते शोकक्रोधग्लपितधृतिरेतस्य सहजः ।
हिरण्यप्रारम्भः कशिपुरमरारातिसदसि
प्रतिज्ञामातेने तव किल वधार्थं मधुरिपो ॥ २४-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Hiranyakshan was killed by lord during Varaha avathaaram, when he came in the form of divine boar. Outraged by the loss of his brother, Hiranyakashipu swore in the kingdom of Asuras to kill the Lord in revenge.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
hiraṇyākṣe potripravaravapuṣā deva bhavatā
hate śokakrodhaglapitadhṛtiretasya sahajaḥ |
hiraṇyaprārambhaḥ kaśipuramarārātisadasi
pratijñāmātene tava kila vadhārthaṃ madhuripo || 24-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
विधातारं घोरं स खलु तपसित्वा न चिरतः
पुरः साक्षात्कुर्वन् सुरनरमृगाद्यैरनिधनम् ।
वरं लब्ध्वा दृप्तो जगदिह भवन्नायकमिदं
परिक्षुन्दन्निन्द्रादहरत दिवं त्वामगणयन् ॥ २४-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: He quickly compelled Brahmaa to appear before him by performing severe austerities and made him give a boon that he would not be killed by God, man or beast etc. Receiving the boons, Hiranyakashipu tortured the deva loka and took control of the heaven from Indra.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
vidhātāraṃ ghoraṃ sa khalu tapasitvā na cirataḥ
puraḥ sākṣātkurvan suranaramṛgādyairanidhanam |
varaṃ labdhvā dṛpto jagadiha bhavannāyakamidaṃ
parikṣundannindrādaharata divaṃ tvāmagaṇayan || 24-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
निहन्तुं त्वां भूयस्तव पदमवाप्तस्य च रिपो-
-र्बहिर्दृष्टेरन्तर्दधिथ हृदये सूक्ष्मवपुषा ।
नदन्नुच्चैस्तत्राप्यखिलभुवनान्ते च मृगयन्
भिया यातं मत्वा स खलु जितकाशी निववृते ॥ २४-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Hiranyakashipu went in search of Bhagwan in vaikunta, but Bhagwan disappeared from his vision and entered his heart. Roaring aloud he searched for Bhagwan in all the three worlds, not finding Bhagwan, he thought Bhagwan fled in fear and considered that he won and returned back.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
nihantuṃ tvāṃ bhūyastava padamavāptasya ca ripo-
-rbahirdṛṣṭerantardadhitha hṛdaye sūkṣmavapuṣā |
nadannuccaistatrāpyakhilabhuvanānte ca mṛgayan
bhiyā yātaṃ matvā sa khalu jitakāśī nivavṛte || 24-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
ततोऽस्य प्रह्लादः समजनि सुतो गर्भवसतौ
मुनेर्वीणापाणेरधिगतभवद्भक्तिमहिमा ।
स वै जात्या दैत्यः शिशुरपि समेत्य त्वयि रतिं
गतस्त्वद्भक्तानां वरद परमोदाहरणताम् ॥ २४-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: To him was born a son named Prahlaad. Even when he was in the womb, he had learnt the glory of devotion to Bhagwan from sage Naarada. Though by birth he was an Asura, and just a child, he had intense love for Bhagwan and became the most outstanding example for all devotees.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tato’sya prahlādaḥ samajani suto garbhavasatau
munervīṇāpāṇeradhigatabhavadbhaktimahimā |
sa vai jātyā daityaḥ śiśurapi sametya tvayi ratiṃ
gatastvadbhaktānāṃ varada paramodāharaṇatām || 24-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
सुरारीणां हास्यं तव चरणदास्यं निजसुते
स दृष्ट्वा दुष्टात्मा गुरुभिरशिशिक्षच्चिरममुम् ।
गुरुप्रोक्तं चासाविदमिदमभद्राय दृढमि-
-त्यपाकुर्वन् सर्वं तव चरणभक्त्यैव ववृधे ॥ २४-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The evil minded Hiranyakashipu assigned teachers for Prahlaad to brain wash because he saw signs of devotion to Bhagwan. He however rejected all their teachings and was interested in only devotion to Bhagwan.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
surārīṇāṃ hāsyaṃ tava caraṇadāsyaṃ nijasute
sa dṛṣṭvā duṣṭātmā gurubhiraśiśikṣacciramamum |
guruproktaṃ cāsāvidamidamabhadrāya dṛḍhami-
-tyapākurvan sarvaṃ tava caraṇabhaktyaiva vavṛdhe || 24-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अधीतेषु श्रेष्ठं किमिति परिपृष्टेऽथ तनये
भवद्भक्तिं वर्यामभिगदति पर्याकुलधृतिः ।
गुरुभ्यो रोषित्वा सहजमतिरस्येत्यभिविदन्
वधोपायानस्मिन् व्यतनुत भवत्पादशरणे ॥ २४-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Hiranyakashipu asked Prahalaad, what was the best lesson he had learnt. The boy replied that only devotion to Bhagwan was the greatest. Hearing this, Hiranyakashipu was very angry with the teachers, but they told him that this was his son's natural inclination. The furious father plotted ways to kill Prahlaad.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
adhīteṣu śreṣṭhaṃ kimiti paripṛṣṭe’tha tanaye
bhavadbhaktiṃ varyāmabhigadati paryākuladhṛtiḥ |
gurubhyo roṣitvā sahajamatirasyetyabhividan
vadhopāyānasmin vyatanuta bhavatpādaśaraṇe || 24-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
स शूलैराविद्धः सुबहु मथितो दिग्गजगणै-
-र्महासर्पैर्दष्टोऽप्यनशनगराहारविधुतः ।
गिरीन्द्रावक्षिप्तोऽप्यहह परमात्मन्नयि विभो
त्वयि न्यस्तात्मत्वात् किमपि न निपीडामभजत ॥ २४-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Though Prahalaad was pierced with tridents many times, trampled again and again by herds of huge elephants, bitten by great serpents, starved, poisoned and thrown down from the mountain peaks, he did not feel any suffering as his mind was completely fixed on Bhagwan. What a wonder!
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sa śūlairāviddhaḥ subahu mathito diggajagaṇai-
-rmahāsarpairdaṣṭo’pyanaśanagarāhāravidhutaḥ |
girīndrāvakṣipto’pyahaha paramātmannayi vibho
tvayi nyastātmatvāt kimapi na nipīḍāmabhajata || 24-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
ततः शङ्काविष्टः स पुनरतिदुष्टोऽस्य जनको
गुरूक्त्या तद्गेहे किल वरुणपाशैस्तमरुणत् ।
गुरोश्चासान्निध्ये स पुनरनुगान् दैत्यतनयान्
भवद्भक्तेस्तत्त्वं परममपि विज्ञानमशिषत् ॥ २४-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The very cruel father was frightened at this. At the advice of the teacher, Prahlaad was tied up with ropes at the teacher's house. But whenever the teacher was away, Prahlaad began to teach the asura children, the benefits of devotion and knowledge of Bhagwan.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tataḥ śaṅkāviṣṭaḥ sa punaratiduṣṭo’sya janako
gurūktyā tadgehe kila varuṇapāśaistamaruṇat |
guroścāsānnidhye sa punaranugān daityatanayān
bhavadbhaktestattvaṃ paramamapi vijñānamaśiṣat || 24-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
पिता शृण्वन् बालप्रकरमखिलं त्वत् स्तुतिपरं
रुषान्धः प्राहैनं कुलहतक कस्ते बलमिति ।
बलं मे वैकुण्ठस्तव च जगतां चापि स बलं
स एव त्रैलोक्यं सकलमिति धीरोऽयमगदीत् ॥ २४-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: On hearing that Prahalaad is making all the asura children sing in praise of Lord, Hiranyakashipu became very angry. He questioned the boy from where he gets this strength. The boy replied that Bhagwan Vishnu is his strength, He is the strength for Hiranyakashipu and for the universe. The three worlds are nothing but Bhagwan Vishnu.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
pitā śṛṇvan bālaprakaramakhilaṃ tvat stutiparaṃ
ruṣāndhaḥ prāhainaṃ kulahataka kaste balamiti |
balaṃ me vaikuṇṭhastava ca jagatāṃ cāpi sa balaṃ
sa eva trailokyaṃ sakalamiti dhīro’yamagadīt || 24-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अरे क्वासौ क्वासौ सकलजगदात्मा हरिरिति
प्रभिन्ते स्म स्तम्भं चलितकरवालो दितिसुतः ।
अतः पश्चाद्विष्णो न हि वदितुमीशोऽस्मि सहसा
कृपात्मन् विश्वात्मन् पवनपुरवासिन् मृडय माम् ॥ २४-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Hiranyakashipu questioned Prahalaad as to who is Hari? Where is Hari? In a fit of anger, he struck the pillar with his mighty sword. What came out of the pillar and what happened next?!
Bhattadiri was unable to describe and took solace at the feet of Lord Guruvayoorappan.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
are kvāsau kvāsau sakalajagadātmā haririti
prabhinte sma stambhaṃ calitakaravālo ditisutaḥ |
ataḥ paścādviṣṇo na hi vaditumīśo’smi sahasā
kṛpātman viśvātman pavanapuravāsin mṛḍaya mām || 24-10 ||
